23	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
24	
25	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
26	
27	Install the skill:
28	
29	```bash filename="Terminal"
30	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
31	```
32	
33	Then give the agent this prompt:
34	
35	```prompt
36	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
37	```
38	
39	## Or adopt by hand
40	
41	To adopt an existing app by hand:
42	
43	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
44	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
45	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
46	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
47	
48	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
49	
50	## Enable Partial Prefetching
51	
52	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
53	
54	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
55	
56	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
57	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
58	
59	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
60	  cacheComponents: true,
61	  partialPrefetching: true,
62	}
63	
64	export default nextConfig
65	```
66	
67	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
68	
69	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
70	
71	## What changes for `<Link>`
72	
73	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
74	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
75	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
76	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
78	
79	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
80	
81	## Migrate existing full prefetches
82	
83	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
84	
85	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
86	
87	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
88	
89	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
90	
91	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
92	
93	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
94	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
95	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
96	
97	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
98	  await page.goto('/products')
99	
100	  await instant(page, async () => {
101	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
102	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
103	    await link.click()
104	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
105	
106	    await expect(
107	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
108	    ).toBeVisible()
109	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
110	  })
111	})
112	```
113	
114	Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
115	
116	### Static or cached content
117	
118	The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:
119	
120	```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"
121	// Before
122	<Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
123	// After
124	<Link href="/about">About</Link>
125	```
126	
127	### Uncached content
128	
129	Cache it with `use cache` so it gets included in the App Shell, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:

135	  return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
136	}
137	```

267	### URL data
268	
269	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
270	
271	### Real-time content
272	
273	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
274	
275	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
276	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
277	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
278	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
279	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
280	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
281	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
282	
283	## Adopting incrementally
284	
285	Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.

592	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
593	
594	## What "instant" means
595	
596	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
597	
598	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
599	
600	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
601	
602	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
603	
604	<details>
605	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
606	
607	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
608	
609	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
610	
611	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during prerendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
612	
613	</details>
614	
615	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
616

651	## The tools
652	
653	### Build the static shell
654	
655	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
656	
657	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
658	
659	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
660	
661	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
662	
663	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `<Link>` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data.
664	
665	### Prefetch URL data for a link
666	
667	Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link.
668	
669	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
670	
671	```tsx
672	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
673	  Checkout
674	</Link>
675	```
676	
677	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
678	
679	### Validate instant navigation
680	
681	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
682	
683	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
684	
685	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
686	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
687	
688	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
689	  cacheComponents: true,
690	  experimental: {
691	    instantInsights: {
692	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
693	    },
694	  },
695	}
696	
697	export default nextConfig
698	```
699	
700	<details>
701	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
702	
703	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
704	
705	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
706	
707	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
708	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
709	
710	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
711	
712	</details>

726	## A page that navigates instantly
727	
728	To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant.
729	
730	The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory.

732	- There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time
733	- Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Each has its own `<Suspense>` boundary
734	- **Product info** rarely changes and is queried from the db using a cached function
735	- **Inventory** must be fresh on each request. The db query is inside a `<Suspense>` boundary

886	## Prevent regressions with e2e tests
887	
888	Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship.
889	
890	The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`:
891	
892	```bash package="pnpm"
893	pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
894	```
895	
896	```bash package="npm"
897	npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
898	```
899	
900	```bash package="yarn"
901	yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
902	```
903	
904	```bash package="bun"
905	bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
906	```

908	A route can be reached two ways, and a `<Suspense>` boundary can cover one without covering the other:
909	
910	- **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response.
911	- **Client navigation**: Click a `<Link>` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI.

915	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'

917	test.describe('Product page (/store/[slug])', () => {
918	  test('is instant on an initial page load', async ({ page, baseURL }) => {
919	    await instant(
920	      page,
921	      async () => {
922	        await page.goto('/store/hats')

929	  })
930

933	    await instant(page, async () => {
934	      await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]')
935	      await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/store/hats')
936	      await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
937	      await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)

1097	### Iterate on loading states
1098	
1099	{/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */}
1100	
1101	Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `<Suspense>` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation.
1102	
1103	The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time.
1104	
1105	Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent.

1107	## AI workflow
1108	
1109	At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this:
1110	
1111	- **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately.
1112	- **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route.
1113	- **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or `<Suspense>`). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation.
1114	- **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard.
1115	
1116	The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `<Suspense>` rather than guessing a cache lifetime.
1117	
1118	For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down.
1119	
1120	Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers:
1121	
1122	- **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell.
1123	- **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile.
1124	- **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it.
1125	
1126	Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect.
1127	
1128	For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `<Suspense>` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup.
1129	
1130	The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both.

1180	
1181	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
1182	
1183	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):
1184	
1185	1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
1186	2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.
1187	3. When the user follows the link, the navigation renders the rest of the route.
1188	
1189	Use [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) to move expensive work to a later stage. To require that a stage stays static across a route, see [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static).

1222	## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
1223	
1224	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
1225	
1226	For a custom link, call `router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })` to request the same per-link stage. Calling `router.prefetch(href)` without the `kind` option requests only the App Shell.
1227	
1228	A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
1229	
1230	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
1231	import Link from 'next/link'
1232	
1233	export default function Home() {
1234	  return (
1235	    <nav>
1236	      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
1237	        React
1238	      </Link>
1239	      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
1240	        Next.js
1241	      </Link>
1242	    </nav>
1243	  )
1244	}
1245	```
1246	
1247	`'auto'` is equivalent to omitting `prefetch` or passing `undefined`. In a conditional expression, return `'auto'` for links that should keep the default App Shell prefetch:
1248	
1249	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
1250	<Link href={href} prefetch={isFeatured ? true : 'auto'} />
1251	```
1252	
1253	Use `prefetch={false}` only when you want to disable prefetching for a link.
1254	
1255	The `/search` page renders a static heading and a `<Results>` list based on the query. The `search()` function caches results by query so later requests can reuse them.
1256	
1257	```tsx filename="app/search/page.tsx"
1258	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1259	
1260	export default function SearchPage({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/search'>) {
1261	  return (
1262	    <>
1263	      <h1>Search</h1>
1264	      <Suspense fallback={<ResultsSkeleton />}>
1265	        <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
1266	      </Suspense>
1267	    </>
1268	  )
1269	}
1270	
1271	async function Results({
1272	  searchParams,
1273	}: {
1274	  searchParams: PageProps<'/search'>['searchParams']
1275	}) {
1276	  const { q } = await searchParams
1277	  return <ResultList items={await search(q)} />
1278	}
1279	
1280	async function search(q: string) {
1281	  'use cache'
1282	  return db.search(q)
1283	}
1284	```
1285	
1286	Without `prefetch={true}`, the App Shell renders `<h1>` and shows the `<Results>` fallback. The query resolves after the click and streams the results in.
1287	
1288	With `prefetch={true}` on the link, the router requests a per-link prefetch that resolves `<Results>` before the click. The `q` value comes from the link's URL, which is known at prefetch time, and the cached `search(q)` call provides the result. When the user clicks, the results render immediately without showing the fallback.
1289	
1290	Next.js includes static and cached content in the prefetch until it reaches an uncached read. It then includes the fallback from the surrounding `<Suspense>` boundary. That boundary is already in place from [structuring the route for instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation).
1291	
1292	Generating the per-link prefetch costs **a server invocation per prefetchable link**, so it is opt-in per link. On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves the prefetch from the static cache instead. A page that accesses non-static data is generated per prefetch, unless that access is [deferred to the navigation](#keep-the-prefetch-static).
1293	
1294	> **Good to know:** A cold cache (first visit, or after expiration) means the server still has to compute the cached result. Users may see a loading spinner on that first navigation. Subsequent navigations are instant as long as the cache is warm.
1295	
1296	Like `searchParams`, `params` needs a `<Suspense>` boundary, even when the values are predefined by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params). A statically known param still belongs to one URL. A per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}` resolves the values `generateStaticParams` does not cover.
1297	
1298	## Include session data in the shell
1299	
1300	`prefetch={true}` resolves URL data. Session data is handled separately. A route that reads `cookies()` or `headers()`, including through `"use cache: private"`, gets an App Shell that includes its session data, cached per session on the client and ready on navigation without a per-link prefetch.
1301	
1302	A lookup based on session data needs a cache lifetime, the same way `search(q)` did for the URL. Take a dashboard nav that reads a cookie, then looks up content based on it:
1303	
1304	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
1305	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1306	
1307	export default function DashboardLayout({
1308	  children,
1309	}: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) {
1310	  return (
1311	    <div>
1312	      <Suspense fallback={<nav>Loading...</nav>}>
1313	        <UserNav />
1314	      </Suspense>
1315	      <main>{children}</main>
1316	    </div>
1317	  )
1318	}
1319	```
1320	
1321	The App Shell render can read session data. However, `"use cache"` cannot call `cookies()` inside the cached function, so use one of these patterns:
1322	
1323	- **Extract and pass** when the lookup result is shared across many sessions.
1324	- **`"use cache: private"`** when it is tied to one.
1325	
1326	### Extract and pass
1327	
1328	Read the cookie outside the cached function and pass the value in as an argument. The `cookies()` call stays outside the cache scope, the argument crosses the boundary, and the cached function has a deterministic signature. The cache entry is keyed on that argument, and sessions that share the value share the entry.
1329	
1330	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/user-nav.tsx"
1331	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1332	
1333	async function UserNav() {
1334	  const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
1335	  const topics = await getTopics(team)
1336	  return (
1337	    <nav>
1338	      {topics.map((topic) => (
1339	        <a key={topic.id} href={topic.href}>
1340	          {topic.label}
1341	        </a>
1342	      ))}
1343	    </nav>
1344	  )
1345	}
1346	
1347	async function getTopics(team: string | undefined) {
1348	  'use cache'
1349	  return db.topics.forTeam(team)
1350	}
1351	```
1352	
1353	On a direct visit, `<UserNav>` shows its fallback until the lookup resolves. On navigation, the App Shell has already resolved it, because the team cookie is session data the shell can read. Because sessions on the same team share the cache entry, traffic to the underlying data scales with team count, not session count.
1354	
1355	Anything without a caching directive still streams in after navigation. A shell holds only what can be prepared ahead of the navigation, not the whole page. It advances only as far as the caching structure allows.
1356	
1357	### `"use cache: private"`
1358	
1359	When the lookup is tied to a single session, use [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). It assigns a cache lifetime to a function that reads cookies, headers, or other runtime data directly. Results are cached in the browser only, scoped to that session.
1360	
1361	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/user-nav.tsx"
1362	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1363	
1364	async function UserNav() {
1365	  const user = await getUser()
1366	  return <nav>{user.name}</nav>
1367	}
1368	
1369	async function getUser() {
1370	  'use cache: private'
1371	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
1372	  return db.users.findBySession(session)
1373	}
1374	```
1375	
1376	Here `cookies()` lives inside the cached function, which only works under `"use cache: private"`. Use the same pattern when runtime data cannot be extracted at the call site. For example, an authentication helper may compare `Date.now()` with a token's expiration, or a session helper may read cookies within its own code.
1377	
1378	Everything inside the scope shares the same lifetime. Colocate `"use cache: private"` as close to the runtime data access as possible.
1379	
1380	## Defer work to a later stage
1381	
1382	The App Shell is shared by the links into a route. A per-link prefetch runs for a visible `<Link prefetch={true}>` or a manual `router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })` call, and the navigation runs when the user clicks. Expensive work may not be worth generating for links the user never follows.
1383	
1384	Uncached work is already left out of prefetches. For cacheable work, `next/cache` exports functions that defer the code below each call:
1385	
1386	- [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) defers the code until a per-link prefetch or navigation.
1387	- [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) defers the code until navigation.
1388	
1389	In the following diagram, a gray dashed outline marks the Suspense fallback, while blue marks the deferred work once it renders:
1390	
1391	<Image
1392	  alt="The Shell, Prefetch, and Navigation stages, with bars showing that work below prefetch() renders from the per-link prefetch onward and work below navigation() renders only during navigation, while earlier stages show the Suspense fallback"
1393	  srcLight="/docs/light/navigation-stage-visual.png"
1394	  srcDark="/docs/dark/navigation-stage-visual.png"
1395	  width="1200"
1396	  height="480"
1397	/>
1398	
1399	Both functions apply only during runtime rendering, so they do not change a fully static route. Each call defers the component that awaits it and that component's descendants. Earlier stages render the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) fallback, which the deferred subtree replaces when its stage runs. Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), neither function makes the subtree request-dependent, so functions within it can still use `use cache`. See [How `navigation()` differs from `connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation#how-navigation-differs-from-connection).
1400	
1401	### Keep expensive session data out of the App Shell
1402	
1403	Take the dashboard again. A ranking keyed on the session is expensive, and every default `<Link>` into the dashboard would generate it for the shell. Await `prefetch()` above the ranking so that only a `<Link prefetch={true}>` resolves it before the click:
1404	
1405	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/recommendations.tsx" highlight={6}
1406	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1407	import { prefetch } from 'next/cache'
1408	
1409	async function Recommendations() {
1410	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
1411	  await prefetch()
1412	  const items = await rank(session)
1413	  return <List items={items} />
1414	}
1415	
1416	async function rank(session?: string) {
1417	  'use cache: private'
1418	  return db.recommendations.rank({ session })
1419	}
1420	```
1421	
1422	The session is read above `prefetch()`, so it still resolves in the shell. The App Shell does not generate the ranking. A default `<Link>` includes the `<Suspense>` fallback, which the ranking replaces during navigation. A `<Link prefetch={true}>` resolves the ranking before the click. `rank` keeps its cache lifetime in both cases.
1423	
1424	Neither function can be awaited inside a cached scope, so the directive goes on a function called below it, as `rank` does here.
1425	
1426	### Wait for the navigation
1427	
1428	Consider an inbox where each visible thread uses `<Link prefetch={true}>`. The prefetch should include the thread subject, but fetching every message body before the user opens it would waste work.
1429	
1430	Render the latest message in its own `<Suspense>` boundary and await `navigation()` before loading it:
1431	
1432	```tsx filename="app/inbox/[threadId]/thread.tsx" highlight={19}
1433	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1434	import { navigation } from 'next/cache'
1435	import { getLatestMessage, getThreadSummary } from '@/lib/mail'
1436	
1437	export async function Thread({ threadId }: { threadId: string }) {
1438	  const thread = await getThreadSummary(threadId)
1439	
1440	  return (
1441	    <article>
1442	      <h1>{thread.subject}</h1>
1443	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading message...</p>}>
1444	        <LatestMessage threadId={threadId} />
1445	      </Suspense>
1446	    </article>
1447	  )
1448	}
1449	
1450	async function LatestMessage({ threadId }: { threadId: string }) {
1451	  await navigation()
1452	  const message = await getLatestMessage(threadId)
1453	  return <p>{message.body}</p>
1454	}
1455	```
1456	
1457	Both queries remain cached:
1458	
1459	```ts filename="lib/mail.ts"
1460	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
1461	
1462	export async function getThreadSummary(threadId: string) {
1463	  'use cache'
1464	  return db.thread.findUniqueOrThrow({
1465	    select: { subject: true },
1466	    where: { id: threadId },
1467	  })
1468	}
1469	
1470	export async function getLatestMessage(threadId: string) {
1471	  'use cache'
1472	  return db.message.findFirstOrThrow({
1473	    orderBy: { sentAt: 'desc' },
1474	    select: { body: true },
1475	    where: { threadId },
1476	  })
1477	}
1478	```
1479	
1480	The per-link prefetch includes the cached subject and the message fallback. The cached message body loads when the user opens the thread, then remains available for later visits.
1481	
1482	{/* TODO: once `<Link prefetch="navigation">` ships, document it here as the opt-in for a link that also prefetches cacheable work deferred with `navigation()`. */}
1483	
1484	Leaving the subtree uncached would also keep it out of prefetches, but it would lose its cache lifetime on navigation too. For `use cache` content, a [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time of five minutes or more lets the client-side router reuse it after the first navigation. Below that, each navigation fetches it again.
1485	
1486	### Keep the prefetch static
1487	
1488	When every read of `cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, and `searchParams` sits below `navigation()`, a runtime prefetch would produce the same output as the build. Next.js can therefore serve the prefetch from static output. A CDN can cache that output, so a link into the route requires no server compute.
1489	
1490	The dashboard cannot take this shape, because `<UserNav>` reads the team cookie in the shell. A feed with a static header can:
1491	
1492	```tsx filename="app/feed/page.tsx" highlight={17}
1493	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1494	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1495	import { navigation } from 'next/cache'
1496	
1497	export default function Page() {
1498	  return (
1499	    <>
1500	      <FeedHeader /> {/* static, and so is the whole prefetch */}
1501	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading stories...</p>}>
1502	        <Stories />
1503	      </Suspense>
1504	    </>
1505	  )
1506	}
1507	
1508	async function Stories() {
1509	  await navigation()
1510	  const topic = (await cookies()).get('topic')?.value ?? 'all'
1511	  return <StoryList items={await getStories(topic)} />
1512	}
1513	```
1514	
1515	Reading the cookie below `navigation()` does not make the per-link prefetch render per request, because that read would not have resolved during the prefetch anyway. The same holds for `prefetch()` and the App Shell. When every `cookies()` and `headers()` read sits below `prefetch()`, the shell is served from static output. Reading `params` or `searchParams` does not require a runtime shell. URL data is excluded from the shared shell, but it can make a per-link prefetch render at runtime unless it sits below `navigation()`.
1516	
1517	Each call defers one subtree. To require static output for the whole route, so a later change cannot reintroduce request-time rendering, set [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic). The [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) guide walks through each level.
1518	
1519	## Test prefetched and deferred content
1520	
1521	The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) explains how to install and configure `@next/playwright`. For a client navigation, use `instant()` to inspect the destination's prefetched UI.
1522	
1523	When [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests), run this test before enabling the feature and rerun the same assertions afterward. This preserves the UI selected from the legacy full prefetch while its implementation moves to the App Shell or a per-link prefetch.
1524	
1525	Inside the callback, click the link, wait for the destination URL, and assert which content is available. After the callback releases the navigation, assert that deferred content eventually renders:
1526	
1527	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={8-15,17}
1528	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
1529	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
1530	
1531	test('prefetches the product summary but not reviews', async ({ page }) => {
1532	  await page.goto('/products')
1533	
1534	  await instant(page, async () => {
1535	    await page.click('a[href="/products/baseball-cap"]')
1536	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
1537	
1538	    await expect(
1539	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
1540	    ).toBeVisible()
1541	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
1542	    await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toHaveCount(0)
1543	  })
1544	
1545	  await expect(page.getByTestId('reviews')).toBeVisible()
1546	})
1547	```
1548	
1549	While the `instant()` callback is running, dynamic content is paused. In this example, the product summary is part of the prefetched UI, while reviews wait for navigation. The final assertion confirms that the reviews render after the pause is released.
1550	
1551	In development, a `prefetch()` or `navigation()` call outside `<Suspense>` surfaces an [Instant Insight](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage). A fully prerendered route is unaffected, but the insight identifies that the call would defer content without a fallback if the route later requires runtime rendering. Calls in [`generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage-metadata) and [`generateViewport()`](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage-viewport) have separate insights.
1552	
1553	## Trade-offs
1554	
1555	Use `prefetch={true}` on routes where:
1556	
1557	- Part of the component tree depends on URL data: the full URL, `searchParams`, or `params` not resolved by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)
1558	- That part of the tree has a known cache lifetime (it can be expressed with `"use cache"` or `"use cache: private"`)
1559	- The traffic justifies the per-link server invocation
1560	
1561	Prefetching cached data does not change its freshness behavior. If a mutation can update the data, [tag and invalidate the cached result](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating).
1562	
1563	Skip it when the prefetch can't produce a better UI than the App Shell. Each visible `<Link prefetch={true}>` can wake a server, and that cost only pays off if more of the page is ready before the click:
1564	
1565	- The route has little or no URL-data dependency. The App Shell already makes the navigation instant.
1566	- The dependent content has to be fresh on every request. The prerender stops at the same `<Suspense>` fallback, so the user sees the same UI either way.
1567	- The route is rarely navigated to. You pay per visible link, regardless of click-through.
1568	
1569	A per-link prefetch is best-effort. It only helps the navigations where it completes before the click. On a slow connection, on a feed of many links, or on a direct visit, it may not be ready when the user navigates, and the navigation falls back to the App Shell.
1570	
1571	When many links to a route are visible at once, such as a grid of cards, each `<Link prefetch={true}>` prefetches that link's content as it enters the viewport, so the grid makes one such server request per card. Prefetch on intent instead. A [hover-triggered prefetch](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#hover-triggered-prefetch) fetches only the links the user is likely to click. The default `<Link>` (without `prefetch={true}`) loads only the App Shell, so it doesn't carry this cost.
1572	
1573	|         | App Shell                                                                                 | Per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}`                                                          | Navigation                                           |
1574	| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
1575	| Scope   | One per route                                                                             | One per visible `<Link prefetch={true}>`                                                          | One per click                                        |
1576	| Content | Route's rendered output minus per-link data and work below `prefetch()` or `navigation()` | App Shell plus per-link URL data and work below `prefetch()`, excluding work below `navigation()` | Everything left, including work below `navigation()` |
1577	| Cost    | Bounded by route count                                                                    | Bounded by visible-link count                                                                     | Bounded by navigations                               |
1578	| Role    | Default prefetch                                                                          | More rendered before click                                                                        | Completes the route                                  |
1579	
1580	[Deferring work](#defer-work-to-a-later-stage) avoids generating content for prefetches that may never be used. The tradeoff is that a navigation may show the nearest `<Suspense>` fallback while the deferred content renders.
1581	
1582	## Next steps
1583	
1584	- [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for how `<Link>` behaves under the new model and how to migrate existing apps.
1585	- [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) for the full behavior of each navigation stage API.
1586	- [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) for requiring a static App Shell, prefetch, or complete route with `ensureStatic`.
1587	- [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for validating the route's caching structure.

14	
15	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
16	
17	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
18	
19	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
20	
21	> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
22	
23	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
24	
25	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
26	
27	Install the skill:
28	
29	```bash filename="Terminal"
30	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
31	```
32	
33	Then give the agent this prompt:
34	
35	```prompt
36	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
37	```
38	
39	## Or adopt by hand
40	
41	To adopt an existing app by hand:
42	
43	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
44	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
45	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
46	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
47	
48	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
49	
50	## Enable Partial Prefetching
51	
52	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
53	
54	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
55	
56	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
57	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
58	
59	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
60	  cacheComponents: true,
61	  partialPrefetching: true,
62	}
63	
64	export default nextConfig
65	```
66	
67	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
68	
69	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
70	
71	## What changes for `<Link>`
72	
73	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
74	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
75	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
76	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
78	
79	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
80	
81	## Migrate existing full prefetches
82	
83	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
84	
85	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
86	
87	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
88	
89	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
90	
91	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
92	
93	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
94	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
95	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
96	
97	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
98	  await page.goto('/products')
99

267	### URL data
268	
269	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. 271	### Real-time content
272	
273	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
274	
275	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
276	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
277	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
278	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
279	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
280	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
281	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

592	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
593	
594	## What "instant" means
595	
596	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
597	
598	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
599	
600	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
601	
602	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
603	
604	<details>
605	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
606	
607	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
608	
609	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
610	
611	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during prerendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
612	
613	</details>
614	
615	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
616

653	### Build the static shell
654	
655	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
656	
657	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
658	
659	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
660	
661	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
662	
663	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `<Link>` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data.
664	
665	### Prefetch URL data for a link
666	
667	Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link.
668	
669	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
670	
671	```tsx
672	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
673	  Checkout
674	</Link>
675	```
676	
677	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
678	
679	### Validate instant navigation
680	
681	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
682	
683	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
684	
685	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
686	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
687	
688	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
689	  cacheComponents: true,
690	  experimental: {
691	    instantInsights: {
692	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
693	    },
694	  },
695	}
696	
697	export default nextConfig
698	```
699	
700	<details>
701	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
702	
703	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
704	
705	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
706	
707	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
708	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
709	
710	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
711	
712	</details>

726	## A page that navigates instantly
727	
728	To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant.
729	
730	The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory.
731	
732	- There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time
733	- Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Each has its own `<Suspense>` boundary
734	- **Product info** rarely changes and is queried from the db using a cached function
735	- **Inventory** must be fresh on each request. The db query is inside a `<Suspense>` boundary

744	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading product...</p>}>
745	        <ProductInfo params={props.params} />
746	      </Suspense>

748	        <Inventory params={props.params} />

754	type Params = PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>['params']
755	
756	async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Params }) {
757	  const { slug } = await params
758	  const product = await getProduct(slug)
759	  return (

762	      <p>${product.price}</p>
763	    </>
764	  )
765	}
766

768	  'use cache'
769	  return db.products.findBySlug(slug)
770	}
771	
772	async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Params }) {
773	  const { slug } = await params

887	
888	Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship.
889	
890	The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`:
891	
892	```bash package="pnpm"
893	pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
894	```
895	
896	```bash package="npm"
897	npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
898	```
899	
900	```bash package="yarn"
901	yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
902	```
903	
904	```bash package="bun"

906	```

908	A route can be reached two ways, and a `<Suspense>` boundary can cover one without covering the other:
909	
910	- **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response.
911	- **Client navigation**: Click a `<Link>` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI.

913	```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" highlight={6-14,20-25}

915	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
916	
917	test.describe('Product page (/store/[slug])', () => {
918	  test('is instant on an initial page load', async ({ page, baseURL }) => {
919	    await instant(
920	      page,
921	      async () => {
922	        await page.goto('/store/hats')
923	        await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
924	        await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)
925	      },
926	      { baseURL }
927	    )
928	    await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible()
929	  })
930	
931	  test('is instant on a client navigation', async ({ page }) => {
932	    await page.goto('/store/shoes')
933	    await instant(page, async () => {
934	      await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]')
935	      await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/store/hats')
936	      await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
937	      await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)
938	    })
939	    await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible()
940	  })

1107	## AI workflow
1108	
1109	At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this:
1110	
1111	- **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately.
1112	- **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route.
1113	- **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or `<Suspense>`). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation.
1114	- **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard.
1115	
1116	The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `<Suspense>` rather than guessing a cache lifetime.
1117	
1118	For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down.
1119	
1120	Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers:
1121	
1122	- **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell.
1123	- **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile.
1124	- **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it.
1125	
1126	Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect.
1127	
1128	For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `<Suspense>` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup.
1129	
1130	The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both.

1132	## Opting out
1133	
1134	Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes.

1158	For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. 1180	
1181	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
1182	
1183	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):
1184	
1185	1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
1186	2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.
1187	3. When the user follows the link, the navigation renders the rest of the route.
1188	
1189	Use [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) to move expensive work to a later stage. To require that a stage stays static across a route, see [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static).

1222	## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
1223	
1224	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
1225	
1226	For a custom link, call `router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })` to request the same per-link stage. Calling `router.prefetch(href)` without the `kind` option requests only the App Shell.
1227	
1228	A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
1229	
1230	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
1231	import Link from 'next/link'
1232	
1233	export default function Home() {
1234	  return (
1235	    <nav>
1236	      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
1237	        React
1238	      </Link>
1239	      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
1240	        Next.js
1241	      </Link>
1242	    </nav>
1243	  )
1244	}
1245	```
1246	
1247	`'auto'` is equivalent to omitting `prefetch` or passing `undefined`. In a conditional expression, return `'auto'` for links that should keep the default App Shell prefetch:
1248	
1249	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
1250	<Link href={href} prefetch={isFeatured ? true : 'auto'} />
1251	```
1252	
1253	Use `prefetch={false}` only when you want to disable prefetching for a link.
1254	
1255	The `/search` page renders a static heading and a `<Results>` list based on the query. The `search()` function caches results by query so later requests can reuse them.
1256	
1257	```tsx filename="app/search/page.tsx"
1258	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1259	
1260	export default function SearchPage({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/search'>) {
1261	  return (
1262	    <>
1263	      <h1>Search</h1>
1264	      <Suspense fallback={<ResultsSkeleton />}>
1265	        <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
1266	      </Suspense>
1267	    </>
1268	  )
1269	}
1270	
1271	async function Results({
1272	  searchParams,
1273	}: {
1274	  searchParams: PageProps<'/search'>['searchParams']
1275	}) {
1276	  const { q } = await searchParams
1277	  return <ResultList items={await search(q)} />
1278	}
1279	
1280	async function search(q: string) {
1281	  'use cache'
1282	  return db.search(q)
1283	}
1284	```
1285	
1286	Without `prefetch={true}`, the App Shell renders `<h1>` and shows the `<Results>` fallback. The query resolves after the click and streams the results in.
1287	
1288	With `prefetch={true}` on the link, the router requests a per-link prefetch that resolves `<Results>` before the click. The `q` value comes from the link's URL, which is known at prefetch time, and the cached `search(q)` call provides the result. When the user clicks, the results render immediately without showing the fallback.
1289	
1290	Next.js includes static and cached content in the prefetch until it reaches an uncached read. It then includes the fallback from the surrounding `<Suspense>` boundary. That boundary is already in place from [structuring the route for instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation).
1291	
1292	Generating the per-link prefetch costs **a server invocation per prefetchable link**, so it is opt-in per link. On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves the prefetch from the static cache instead. A page that accesses non-static data is generated per prefetch, unless that access is [deferred to the navigation](#keep-the-prefetch-static).
1293	
1294	> **Good to know:** A cold cache (first visit, or after expiration) means the server still has to compute the cached result. Users may see a loading spinner on that first navigation. Subsequent navigations are instant as long as the cache is warm.
1295	
1296	Like `searchParams`, `params` needs a `<Suspense>` boundary, even when the values are predefined by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params). A statically known param still belongs to one URL. A per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}` resolves the values `generateStaticParams` does not cover.
